introduction_markdown: Answer any FIVE out of the eight questions. If more than five questions are answered, only the first five will be marked. All questions carry equal marks. Marks allocated to parts of questions are indicated in brackets. Illustrate your answers wherever desirable with large, clear and fully labelled diagrams. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed. Duration: three hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A male aphid homozygous for grey coloured body and long wings was crossed with a female aphid homozygous for white coloured body and short wings. All the 150 off spring obtained possessed grey body and long wings. When the F$_1$ males were mated with females having the female parents' genetic makeup, they produced the following offspring:

- 205 aphids with grey body and long wings
- 16 aphids with grey body and short wings
- 17 aphids with white body and long wings
- 201 aphids with white body and short wings

questions.enonce_markdown: Using suitable genetic symbols, explain these crosses giving the genotypes, phenotypes and proportions of these in the parents and offspring. *[14 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Key.** $G$ = grey body (dominant), $g$ = white body; $L$ = long wings (dominant), $l$ = short wings.

**Observation.** The F$_1$ are all grey and long, so grey and long are dominant. In the test cross the result is **not** the 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio expected for genes on different chromosomes: the two **parental types** (grey long 205, white short 201) are far more numerous than the two **recombinant types** (grey short 16, white long 17). The genes for body colour and wing length are therefore **linked** (on the same chromosome), with a few **crossovers** between them at meiosis.

**Cross 1: the original parents (both homozygous)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parental phenotypes | Male grey body, long wings $\times$ female white body, short wings |
| Parental genotypes | $\dfrac{GL}{GL}$ $\times$ $\dfrac{gl}{gl}$ |
| Gametes | all $GL$ ; all $gl$ |
| F$_1$ genotype | $\dfrac{GL}{gl}$ (heterozygous, $G$ and $L$ on the same chromosome) |
| F$_1$ phenotype and number | all **grey body, long wings** (150 offspring, 100 per cent) |

**Cross 2: F$_1$ male $\times$ female with the genotype of the female parent (test cross)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parental phenotypes | F$_1$ male grey long $\times$ female white short |
| Parental genotypes | $\dfrac{GL}{gl}$ $\times$ $\dfrac{gl}{gl}$ |
| Gametes of the F$_1$ male | **Parental (non-crossover):** $GL$ and $gl$ (large numbers). **Recombinant (crossover):** $Gl$ and $gL$ (few) |
| Gametes of the female | all $gl$ |

**Offspring (test-cross progeny, total 439)**

| Gamete of male $\times$ $gl$ | Genotype | Phenotype | Number | Proportion | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $GL$ | $\dfrac{GL}{gl}$ | grey body, long wings | 205 | 46.7 % | parental |
| $gl$ | $\dfrac{gl}{gl}$ | white body, short wings | 201 | 45.8 % | parental |
| $Gl$ | $\dfrac{Gl}{gl}$ | grey body, short wings | 16 | 3.6 % | recombinant |
| $gL$ | $\dfrac{gL}{gl}$ | white body, long wings | 17 | 3.9 % | recombinant |

The observed numbers are very close to those expected for a crossover value of 7.5 per cent (about 203 : 16 : 16 : 203, i.e. 46.2 : 3.8 : 3.8 : 46.2 per cent), and very different from the 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio (110 of each) expected with independent assortment ($\chi^2 = 317$ with 3 degrees of freedom, far above the 5 per cent critical value of 7.8, so independent assortment is rejected).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Calculate the Cross over Value (CoV) for the two traits involved. *[4 marks]*

(ii) What is the significance of a cross over value (CoV)? *[2 marks]* *(14, 4, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Calculation**

$$\text{Crossover value} = \frac{\text{number of recombinant (crossover) offspring}}{\text{total number of offspring}} \times 100$$

- Recombinants (grey short + white long) $= 16 + 17 = 33$
- Total offspring $= 205 + 16 + 17 + 201 = 439$

$$\text{CoV} = \frac{33}{439} \times 100 = 7.5\%$$

(Check: parental types $= 205 + 201 = 406$, and $\frac{406}{439} \times 100 = 92.5\%$; $92.5\% + 7.5\% = 100\%$.)

**Crossover value = 7.5 per cent** (7.5 map units).

**(ii) Significance**

1. A crossover value **below 50 per cent** shows that the genes are **linked**, that is **on the same chromosome**, and that **crossing over** takes place between them (in 7.5 per cent of the gametes). Unlinked genes give 50 per cent recombinants.
2. The crossover value is **proportional to the distance between the genes** (1 per cent = 1 map unit), so the two genes are **7.5 map units apart** and fairly close; it is used to **construct chromosome (linkage) maps** and to locate genes relative to each other.
3. It allows the **proportion of recombinants** from a cross to be **predicted** (breeders, geneticists).
